newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Safren seeks to reap globalisation benefit.
newsitem.headline: Safren seeks to reap globalisation benefit.

text.p: Investment holding group Safmarine and Rennies Holdings Ltd said it hoped to generate more revenue from abroad in the face of limited opportunity on its home market.

Addressing shareholders after the group's annual general meeting on Wednesday, chairman Buddy Hawton said the global side of Safren's business would continue to play a significant part in its expansion programme.
Through subsidiary Kersaf Investments Ltd, Safren already has extensive casino and hotel interests in the Bahamas, Mauritius, Camores, France and the U.S.
Hawton said "significant" expansion was planned in the Bahamas and the U.S., where Kersaf hoped to get a gaming licence for a resort in Atlantic City within the next week.
He said subsidiary Safmarine's new partnership with Belgian company CMB Transport NV had increased Safren's spread of routes and made it less reliant on trade in and out of South Africa.
"This will allow us to be a major player and as a result we also are looking at another opportunity in terms of a further alliance...which will further broaden our base."
The reefer division, which carried perishable refrigerated cargoes, was also considering a merger with another group to broaden its base.
Hawton said Safren's cinema chain, Interleisure, was examining investment opportunities in eastern Europe and Britain.

He said more than two billion rand had been invested in new ships, containers and aircraft over the last two years to upgrade equipment -- an investment in part prompted by signs of a weakening rand and a softening in the supply market.
"Not that we are forgetting South Africa. It is just that in some of our businesses we are fairly substantial and therefore opportunities become more limited," Hawton said.
These areas included shipping, hotels, casinos and travel services.
Hawton said that the shake-up in the casino industry in particular was expected to affect local operations.
Casinos used to be limited to the former black homelands but the nine new provinces in the reincorprated South Africa now have the right to grant a limited number of casino licences.
Safren would probably have to close some of its operations to accommodate newcomers.
